title: Starbucks’ AI tool didn’t die in a pilot. It died in 11,300 stores.

content_html:
Starbucks told NomadGo on 3 April that it was scrapping the AI inventory tool the Redmond startup had built for it. Within days the 30-person company cut a large part of its workforce, according to GeekWire.

The cuts included the technical team that ran the Starbucks account. Starbucks did not tell its own baristas for another six weeks.

“There’s nothing you can do when leadership and strategy change,” David Greschler, NomadGo’s chief executive, said. He called the decision a complete surprise.

The account comes from a Fast Company investigation published on Monday. It draws on dozens of Starbucks employees and on the startup itself.

We covered the cancellation in May. The vendor’s side of it has been missing until now.

The 💜 of EU tech

The latest rumblings from the EU tech scene, a story from our wise ol' founder Boris, and some questionable AI art. It's free, every week, in your inbox. Sign up now!

Baristas heard on 18 May. The memo told them to pull the QR tracking codes off the backroom shelves and count by hand again.

What actually broke

The failures were mundane and physical. A shift supervisor near Seattle aimed the iPad at a steel fridge. The camera caught the reflection, and five cartons of oat milk registered as ten.

Elsewhere the app marked milks as the wrong type, swapped syrups, and in one photograph counted a bin as food.

A store manager in Graham, Texas, had the opposite problem. Patchy Wi-Fi wiped her count partway through, and her managers had already ruled hand counts unacceptable. That left the store with no usable number at all.

The model was not the problem

NomadGo’s computer vision hit 99% accuracy in controlled tests. Its launch announcement promised counts up to eight times faster than manual methods.

Greschler’s explanation is more interesting than a simple accuracy failure. Computer vision struggles when the inventory itself keeps changing, he said.

Seasonal cups and limited-time packaging could need up to six weeks of retraining. His developers sometimes learned about new items only once they reached the shelves.

The other constraint was older still. People who worked on the tool pointed to the Starbucks backend. It runs on a legacy IBM AS/400 system from the 1990s, which makes real-time store data hard to move.

Insiders estimated the programme may have cost north of $10m over several years.

None of this was a pilot

The Starbucks AI inventory tool, called Automated Counting, reached all 11,300 company-operated cafés in North America by the end of September 2025. It was gone by 18 May.

Enterprise AI failures are usually described as pilots that never scaled. This one scaled first, which is what made being wrong so expensive.

MIT’s NANDA initiative found that 95% of enterprise generative AI pilots delivered no measurable profit impact. Most enterprise AI spending still has not left the lab.

The UK’s Office for National Statistics found the same shape in adoption data, with AI use widening rather than deepening. Starbucks went the other way and went deep everywhere at once.

Starbucks also defended the tool in public shortly before killing it. Reuters reported the miscounts in February, and the company said then that adoption had improved product availability, CNBC reported. Roughly eight weeks later it told NomadGo to stop.

The leadership change Greschler did not name

Greschler blamed a change of leadership and strategy. He did not say which one. The sequence is on the record.

Deb Hall Lefevre, then Starbucks chief technology officer, praised the deployment in NomadGo’s launch release on 3 September 2025.

She resigned on 29 September, the same month the rollout finished. Starbucks hired a permanent replacement from Amazon in December.

The tool outlived its executive sponsor by about six months.

What Starbucks says now

“We use technology to support human connection, not to replace it,” a Starbucks spokesperson told GeekWire. The company pointed to $500m spent on putting more staff in its coffeehouses.

“When it fell short, we listened to feedback and changed course.”

That deserves a fair hearing. Killing a deployed tool across 11,300 sites is harder than letting a pilot quietly expire, and plenty of firms keep paying for software their staff have stopped trusting.

Starbucks has kept its other AI work running. That includes Green Dot Assist for baristas and a ChatGPT integration for customers.

The part the statement does not cover is the supplier. A tool that generates work rather than saving it is a familiar failure, and researchers have given it a name.

Less discussed is who absorbs the cost when a large customer changes its mind. The Starbucks AI inventory tool failed at 11,300 sites, and the bill for that landed on a company of 30 people.

咖啡师于 5 月 18 日举行听证会。 备忘录要求他们将二维码从后台的架子上拉下来，然后再次手工计数。

到底是什么打破了

失败是平凡的和身体上的。 西雅图附近的一名值班主管将 iPad 对准了一台钢制冰箱。 相机捕捉到了倒影，五箱燕麦奶显示为十箱。

在其他地方，该应用程序将牛奶标记为错误类型，交换了糖浆，并在一张照片中将一个垃圾箱算作食物。

德克萨斯州格雷厄姆的一位商店经理遇到了相反的问题。 时断时续的 Wi-Fi 信号使她的计数中途被抹掉，她的经理们已经裁定手工计数不可接受。 这使得商店根本没有可用的号码。

模型不是问题

NomadGo 的计算机视觉在受控测试中达到 99% 的准确率。 其发布公告承诺，计数速度比手动方法快八倍。

格雷施勒的解释比简单的准确性失败更有趣。 他说，当库存本身不断变化时，计算机视觉就会陷入困境。

季节性杯子和限时包装可能需要长达六周的再培训。 他的开发人员有时只有在新产品上架后才了解它们。

另一个限制则更为古老。 开发该工具的人指出了星巴克的后端。 它在 20 世纪 90 年代遗留的 IBM AS/400 系统上运行，这使得实时存储数据难以移动。

业内人士估计，该计划几年内的成本可能超过 1000 万美元。

这些都不是飞行员

截至 2025 年 9 月，星巴克人工智能库存工具“自动盘点”已覆盖北美所有 11,300 家公司运营的咖啡馆。 5月18日就消失了。

企业人工智能失败通常被描述为从未规模化的试点。 这是第一个规模化的，这就是错误如此昂贵的原因。

麻省理工学院的 NANDA 计划发现，95% 的企业生成式人工智能试点项目没有带来可衡量的利润影响。 大多数企业人工智能支出仍然没有离开实验室。

英国国家统计局在采用数据中发现了同样的情况，人工智能的使用范围扩大而不是深化。 星巴克反其道而行之，一下子就深入到各个地方。

星巴克在关闭该工具前不久还公开为其辩护。 据 CNBC 报道，路透社在 2 月份报道了计数错误，该公司当时表示，采用该技术提高了产品可用性。 大约八周后，它告诉 NomadGo 停止。

格雷施勒没有透露领导层变动的名称

格雷施勒将此归咎于领导层和战略的变化。 他没有说是哪一个。 该序列已记录在案。

时任星巴克首席技术官 Deb Hall Lefevre 在 2025 年 9 月 3 日发布的 NomadGo 版本中赞扬了这一部署。

她于 9 月 29 日辞职，同月推出完成。 星巴克去年 12 月从亚马逊聘请了一名永久替代者。

该工具比其执行发起人的寿命多了大约六个月。

星巴克现在说什么

星巴克发言人告诉 GeekWire：“我们使用技术来支持人与人之间的联系，而不是取代它。” 该公司指出，花费了 5 亿美元在其咖啡馆安置更多员工。

“当效果不佳时，我们听取了反馈并改变了方向。”

这值得公正的听证会。 杀死一个在 11,300 个站点部署的工具比让一个试点悄然失效更困难，而且许多公司继续为员工不再信任的软件付费。

星巴克仍在继续其其他人工智能工作。 其中包括为咖啡师提供的 Green Dot Assist 以及为客户提供的 ChatGPT 集成。

该声明未涵盖的部分是供应商。 产生工作而不是保存工作的工具是一种常见的失败，研究人员给它起了一个名字。

较少讨论的是，当大客户改变主意时，谁来承担成本。 星巴克人工智能库存工具在 11,300 个地点失败，而账单落在了一家拥有 30 名员工的公司身上。
